title: A Framework for LLM System Design
summary: A reusable eight-step method for any LLM design question: clarify, estimate, sketch, deep-dive, evaluate, protect, break and trade off. One running example carries real numbers through every step.
objectives: Apply an eight-step framework to an open-ended LLM design prompt and pace it inside 45 minutes
Turn users and behaviour into QPS, peak QPS, tokens per day and a monthly API bill
Size a self-hosted deployment: GPUs, KV-cache memory via Little's law, and embedding storage
Choose deep dives (retrieval, model choice, serving, caching) and justify them with numbers
Write an evaluation, safety and failure-mode plan, and present trade-offs as explicit choices
prerequisites: Comfort with the earlier modules helps, in particular [Measuring Inference](/learn/inference-and-serving/measuring-inference), [Capacity Planning and Cost per Request](/learn/inference-and-serving/capacity-and-cost), [How RAG Works](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/rag-architecture) and [Choosing and Routing Models](/learn/production-systems/model-routing). All prices in this module are hypothetical.
